chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Dharih al-Muharibi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who swore that he would definitely perform Hajj on foot, but he became unable to do so and could not manage it. He (AS) said: 'Then let him ride and bring the offering (Hady).'

The Shaykh (Al-Shaykh Al-Tusi) said (peace be upon him): And if a man travels with his wife in the same riding animal (mahmal), they do not pray together, but if one of them prays and finishes, the other then prays.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who vows to perform Hajj on foot but cannot walk?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of proportional fulfillment in vows (nadhr), where physical inability to walk transforms the obligation into riding with the accompanying sacrifice, reflecting the juristic flexibility of the Imams. The supplementary note on the husband and wife praying separately while sharing a mount highlights the practical application of prayer validity in constrained travel conditions, a detail often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the preservation of prayer integrity during Hajj.
